title: docs(scripts): the $-dialect census keeps its by-name self carve-out, with the reasons pinned (objectui#9891)
body:
Fixes objectstack-ai/objectui#9891

## The judgement: NO — the class does not hold over this instrument. Nothing ported.

Deliverable #1 was a judgement, and the answer is the card's own falsification
condition: `SELF_FILES` here covers the instrument itself, not rows-that-are-data
inside otherwise-ordinary files, so a by-name list is the right tool and the
`fixture-address: REASON` class does not transfer. What landed is the reasoning,
recorded in the docblock, plus three pins that make it falsifiable.

### 1. The class never replaced a self-list — including in the file where it landed

`scripts/cross-file-line-citation-census.mjs` on `main` today still declares its own
`SELF_FILES` (four entries) and `runCensus` still carves those whole files out by
name. objectui#9892's population is 14 addresses in files *outside* that list.
⇒ objectui#9865's ⛔ is against **naming more files** in such a list, ⛔ not against
a self-list existing. Porting here would not remove `SELF_FILES`; it would add a
second mechanism beside it.

### 2. ⭐ There are TWO independent copies in this tree, not three

Measured — every `SELF_FILES` declaration under `scripts/` and `eslint-rules/`:

| site | what it is |
|:--|:--|
| `cross-file-line-citation-census.mjs` | declares the set |
| `dollar-dialect-alias-census.mjs` | declares the set |
| `check-new-cross-file-line-citations.mjs` | **imports** it and re-exports it |

The third is the shared list the citation census's docblock describes on purpose —
"It is one list for BOTH readers ... imports this set rather than keeping a second
copy", stated there *as* the anti-drift argument. Counting it as a copy counts a
user as a duplicate.

### 3. There is nothing here for a per-row declaration to preserve

`roleOf` puts both carved files in role `other`, and `other` is never the number
objectui#8568 asked for (`authored-corpus` is). A spelling written inside this
instrument cannot be an author relying on the tolerance. The property that forced
the declared class — fixture rows sitting *among genuine pointers*, so a whole-file
carve-out hides real rot — this population does not have.

### 4. ⭐ And the asymmetry the card would have found if it had measured

`--- BEFORE (origin/main, fb7dfedbb) --- what each entry actually blocks`

| entry | alias rows | canonical rows | impossible-literal hits |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|
| `scripts/dollar-dialect-alias-census.mjs` | 0 | 1 | **1** |
| `scripts/__tests__/dollar-dialect-alias-census.test.ts` | 0 | 39 | **0** |

Alias rows are 0 because objectui#8568 was ruled (option 1) and the derived alias
set is legitimately empty on this tree; `selfCarved` is therefore 0.

`--- lit control: drop each entry from the carve-out and read the controls ---`

| carve-out | scanned | canonicalRows | controls |
|:--|--:|--:|:--|
| baseline (both entries) | 7856 | 1621 | all four PASS |
| without the census | 7857 | 1622 | **`impossible` FAIL — `$startswithzzz: 1 hit(s)`** |
| without the suite | 7857 | 1660 | all four PASS |
| without both | 7858 | 1661 | **`impossible` FAIL** |

⇒ the census entry is **control-backed**: drift makes the run refuse to print a
number (`main` exits non-zero, "this run is NOT a reading") rather than print a
wrong one. That is the announce-on-drift property a declaration would otherwise
have had to buy — and it is the direction that matters for a report-only census
whose failure mode is a confident wrong number.
⇒ the suite entry is **not** control-backed. Nothing fires.

### 5. ⭐ The docblock was wrong, and so was the pin's justification comment

Both claimed the two files carry the impossible spelling as fixture text. Measured,
`git grep startswithzzz` returns **exactly one** hit tree-wide, in the census only:
the suite deliberately hands the imported `IMPOSSIBLE_SPELLING` binding to
`scanText` instead. The old pin asserted set membership and would have passed
either way. Both comments are corrected per entry, and the corrected claim is now
pinned rather than narrated.

## What landed

- `scripts/dollar-dialect-alias-census.mjs` — the `SELF_FILES` docblock, rewritten
  per entry, plus the recorded judgement so the next sweep does not re-file this;
  and the unreachable `SELF_FILES` arm inside `scannable` annotated as
  belt-and-braces (`runCensus` diverts those rows above its only call), because
  read as a live second judgement site it is exactly what the card counted.
- `scripts/__tests__/dollar-dialect-alias-census.test.ts` — three pins: the
  membership pin, a bait pin (the literal lives in the census and **not** in the
  suite), and an ablation pin that drops each entry from the live set and reads the
  controls — census leg must fire `impossible`, suite leg must fire nothing.

## The ablations — the new pins redden, shown rather than asserted

Both run from the committed tree, restored via `git checkout HEAD -- PATH` in an
`EXIT INT TERM` trap, restore verified by an empty `git diff HEAD` and a blob-hash
match against `HEAD`.

**A — remove the bait**: `IMPOSSIBLE_SPELLING` built by `join('')` instead of a
literal. On-disk proof: literal-bearing lines 1 → 0, injected marker 1.
⇒ `Tests 2 failed | 35 passed (37)`, exit 1 — both new pins red.

**B — give the suite a bait literal**: on-disk proof: bait lines 0 → 1, marker 2.
⇒ `Tests 2 failed | 35 passed (37)`, exit 1, the asymmetry pin reporting
`expected [ 'impossible' ] to deeply equal []` — i.e. leg 2 reddens for exactly the
reason it exists.

Restores verified: both blobs back to `5d8b0020…` / `397664f8…`, `git diff HEAD`
empty.

## Gates, with exit codes

| gate | exit |
|:--|--:|
| `vitest run --project unit scripts/__tests__/dollar-dialect-alias-census.test.ts` — 37 passed (was 35) | 0 |
| `vitest run --project unit` on both citation suites — 101 passed | 0 |
| `pnpm check:control-bytes` | 0 |
| `pnpm check:new-line-citations` — "0 new citation(s)" | 0 |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` — "no changeset is owed" | 0 |
| `pnpm check:test-path-roots` | 0 |
| `pnpm census:dollar-dialect-aliases` — all four controls PASS | 0 |
| `pnpm type-check:scripts` | 0 |
| `pnpm lint:root` — 0 errors, 32 pre-existing warnings, none in the two files | 0 |

Changeset: none owed, and that is **measured**, not asserted — the presence gate
reports 0 of 2 changed files are published source of a released package.
⛔ No new npm script, ⛔ no new CI context, ⛔ no doc edit: `census:dollar-dialect-aliases`
already exists and is unchanged.

## Escalation: ⛔ none. p3 stands.

Triage's condition was a **measured rename drift**. All six paths named across both
`SELF_FILES` declarations are tracked today; no entry is unmatched and none matches
something it should not. "A third copy exists" is the card's premise, not an
escalation reason — and it is also off by one (see §2).

## Acceptance notes

Out of scope, noted, ⛔ not filed:

- The `SELF_FILES` arm inside `scannable` is unreachable from `runCensus` (the only
  call site sits below the divert). Dead-but-defensive code, annotated rather than
  removed — no defect, no card. Successor: whoever next touches this census.
- The suite entry's carve-out rests on the plain argument with no control behind it.
  That is now recorded and pinned, ⛔ not repaired: inventing a control for it would
  be a mechanism this card did not ask for. Successor: none today; the pin turns red
  the day someone adds one, which forces the docblock to be corrected in the same
  change.
